identity.title: An ALMA Survey of Sub-millimeter Galaxies in the Extended Chandra Deep Field South: Sub-millimeter Properties of Color-selected Galaxies

paper_type_evidence.quote: Details on the survey design, on the data reduction and the cleaning process are described in (cite: hodge13).
The data employed in this analysis are available from the ALMA and ESO archives.

targets.name: ALESS fields (LESS sources in the ECDFS)

evidence.quote: We base our study on 344 GHz ALMA continuum observations of $\sim20''$–wide fields centered on 86 sub-mm sources detected in the LABOCA Extended *Chandra* Deep Field South Sub-mm Survey (LESS).

distance_source.value: photometric/spectroscopic redshifts from Simpson et al. 2014

evidence.quote: We base our study on 344 GHz ALMA continuum observations of $\sim20''$–wide fields centered on 86 sub-mm sources detected in the LABOCA Extended *Chandra* Deep Field South Sub-mm Survey (LESS).

question.value: What are the sub-mm (344 GHz) properties, dust SEDs and SFRs of optical/NIR color-selected galaxies (K-selected, sBzK, ERO, DRG) in ALESS fields, as measured by stacking ALMA data?

evidence.quote: We study the sub-mm properties of color–selected galaxies via a stacking analysis applied for the first time to interferometric data at sub-mm wavelengths.
This paper makes use of the following ALMA data: ADS/JAO.ALMA#2011.1.00294.S.
These are 344 GHz observations of 122 sources.

configurations.value: Cycle 0 compact configuration, longest baseline 125 m, mostly 15 antennas

evidence.quote: with the array in ALMA Cycle 0’s compact configuration (longest baseline: 125m), mostly with 15 antennas.
The typical resolution element has a FWHM $\sim1.6''\times1.15''$.
The typical central rms of the final maps is $\approx0.4$ mJy beam$^{-1}$.
Observations were carried out during ALMA Cycle 0 (‘Early Science’) between October 18 and November 3, 2011

provided.value: 250/350/500 um maps for stacking and dust SED

evidence.quote: we repeat our stacking analysis on the *Herschel*/SPIRE maps of the ECDFS at 250, 350, and 500 $\mu$m.

provided.value: 1.4 GHz ECDFS map (Miller et al.) for radio stacking

evidence.quote: The map was obtained with the Very Large Array in extended (A) configuration, yielding a spatial resolution of $2.8''\times1.6''$ over a $32'\times32'$ wide region.
We base our analysis on the photometric catalog by (cite: simpson14), who capitalized on deep, optical/NIR archival data from various surveys of the ECDFS.

what.value: Photometric catalog, SED fits and photometric redshifts of ECDFS

evidence.quote: We base our analysis on the photometric catalog by (cite: simpson14)
We use the deblended SPIRE maps described in (cite: swinbank14).

evidence.loc: 5.3 Comparison with previous results at 870 um
evidence.quote: Table [1](#tab_results) (bottom) reports the stacked fluxes obtained in G10 for their sub-mm faint sample
Data were reduced and cleaned down to a 3-$\sigma$ level using the Common Astronomy Software Application (CASA).
Final maps are $128\times128$ pixel, with a pixel scale of $0.2''$ per pixel.

what.value: ALMA survey design, data reduction and cleaning

evidence.quote: Details on the survey design, on the data reduction and the cleaning process are described in (cite: hodge13).

what.value: Good-quality map selection (rms<0.6 mJy/beam, axis ratio<2)

evidence.quote: we focus only on the 86 ‘good quality’ maps with rms $<0.6$ mJy beam$^{-1}$ and beam axis ratio $<$ 2 (cite: hodge13).

what.value: K<20 selection and color cuts following G10/Daddi04

evidence.quote: Following G10, we focus on the $K_{\rm Vega}<20$ mag (i.e., $K_{\rm AB}<21.83$ mag) galaxies, to ease the comparison with previous studies.

unstated_but_needed: CASA version and calibration details (in Hodge et al. 2013)
Calibrated ALESS image products/primary beam models used
Exact positions of pointings and catalog cross-match details
Fitting method/priors for the modified blackbody and how SPIRE+344 GHz points were weighted
Redshifts used for each galaxy in SED fits
Radio stacking details (map weighting, median stack procedure)
Procedure for rescaling SFRD by ALESS excess

method.value: Color/magnitude cuts on MUSYC catalog: K_Vega<20, sBzK, ERO, DRG

evidence.quote: Distant Red Galaxies (DRGs), defined as $(J-K)>1.32$ (cite: franx03).

key_parameters.value: only sources within 10.4'' (1.2x primary beam radius) of pointing centre

evidence.quote: We keep only sources lying within $1.2\times$ the primary beam radius of each pointing (i.e., within $10.4''$ from each pointing center)

method.value: Cut stamps, primary-beam correct, weighted average (weights = inverse square of PB correction); also median stacks

evidence.quote: We align all the postage stamps, scale them to account for the primary beam attenuation computed at step #2, and then weight-average them.

key_parameters.value: flux cuts of 3.6, 1.8, 1.2 mJy; z>1 subsample; smoothing to 1.6'' circular beam test

evidence.quote: We then progressively lower the flux cutoff to $S_{\nu}$(344 GHz)=$1.8$ mJy and $S_{\nu}$(344 GHz)=$1.2$ mJy, and repeat the experiment.

assumptions.value: all maps have same depth within ~20%

evidence.quote: Our working assumption is that all the maps have the same depth, which is true to within $\sim20$ % accuracy

validation.value: Two independent stacking routines gave consistent results

evidence.quote: The analysis is repeated with two different stacking routines, developed independently within our collaboration, finding consistent results.

method.value: Stack N random positions per sample, 50 iterations; rms of stacked fluxes = noise

evidence.quote: We perform 50 iterations, in order to gauge the variance of the random stacks.
The assumption here is that the maps are mostly “source-free”
we have verified that the average stacked values in the random iterations are always consistent with zero.

analysis_steps.goal: Stack SPIRE maps and fit dust SED, derive L_IR and SFR

method.value: Stack deblended SPIRE residual maps at z>1; fit modified blackbody; integrate 8-1000 um; SFR from Genzel+10 relation

evidence.quote:
We fit the observed SEDs as modified black bodies $S_
u \propto 
u^{ eta} B_
u(T_{m dust})$
$T_{\rm dust}=12-60$ K is the dust temperature, and $\beta=1.4-2.0$ sets the frequency dependence of the dust opacity
This conversion implicitly assumes a (cite: chabrier03) initial mass function.

validation.value: Compared with dust temperatures from other studies

evidence.quote: These values are in agreement with the findings of similar studies

analysis_steps.goal: Test ALESS-field bias with radio stacks, clustering and redshift distributions

method.value: KS tests, Monte-Carlo clustering, 1.4 GHz median stacks, bootstrapping of field medians

evidence.quote: This bootstrapping approach allows us to evaluate whether the discrepancy between the general field and ALESS-covered galaxies can be explained as an accidentally-bright realization

validation.value: ALESS medians >4-sigma outliers vs field bootstrap

evidence.quote: represent $>4$-$\sigma$ outliers compared with the distribution of median stack values derived from bootstrapping the field sample.

method.value: Average SFR x number of galaxies / comoving volume (34000 Mpc^3, 7.0 arcmin^2, 1<z<2.6), scaled down by ALESS radio excess

evidence.quote: We compute SFRDs associated to our sample of galaxies by multiplying the average SFRs by the number of galaxies in each sample, and dividing the resulting ‘total’ SFRs by the volume sampled in our analysis.
Our estimates of the SFRD for $K$-selected galaxies are in broad agreement with previous work in the literature

used_for.value: ALMA data reduction and cleaning (in Hodge et al. 2013)

evidence.quote: Data were reduced and cleaned down to a 3-$\sigma$ level using the Common Astronomy Software Application (CASA).
We find $\beta=1.6$ and $T_{\rm dust}\approx 30$ K in all the cases.
Our analysis covered $74 \times \pi (1.2 \times 17.3/2)^2$ arcsec$^2$ $\approx$ 0.00193 deg$^2$.

findings_qualitative.value: ALMA stacked 344 GHz fluxes are a factor 2-3 higher than single-dish (G10) stacks; a similar excess seen at 1.4 GHz.

evidence.quote: We compare our results with those of previous studies based on single-dish observations at 870 $\mu$m and find that our flux densities are a factor 2–3 higher than previous estimates.

claims.hypothesis: Color-selected galaxies are detectable at 344 GHz by stacking ALMA data
claims.experiment: Weighted and median stacks of K, sBzK, ERO, DRG at ALESS positions
claims.result: >10-sigma detections in all classes; robust to flux cuts
claims.finding: Color-selected galaxies are detected even without individually detected SMGs

evidence.quote: We find clear, $>10$-$\sigma$ detections in the stacked images of all these galaxy classes.

claims.hypothesis: The ALMA-versus-single-dish flux discrepancy reflects intrinsic brightness of galaxies near SMGs
claims.experiment: Radio stacks, clustering, z/luminosity distributions, photo-z association
claims.result: 1.4 GHz fluxes also higher in ALESS fields; clustering consistent with field
claims.finding: Tentative evidence that galaxies associated with SMGs are brighter than average

evidence.quote: Hence we find tentative evidence that galaxies that are associated in projected and redshift space with sub-mm bright sources are brighter than the average population.

claims.hypothesis: Dust SED and SFR of color-selected z>1 galaxies
claims.experiment: SPIRE+ALMA stacks fitted with modified blackbody
claims.result: T_dust≈30 K, beta=1.6, L_IR (5-11)e11 Lsun, SFR 75-140 Msun/yr
claims.finding: Color-selected galaxies contribute one third to one sixth of SFRD at 1<z<2.6

evidence.quote: we find that color–selected galaxies contribute to one third – one sixth of the cosmic star formation rate density at $1<z<2.6$.

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Discrepancy as artifact of single-dish deblending judged unlikely

evidence.loc: 5.3 Comparison with previous results at 870 um
evidence.quote: The first scenario seems unlikely, given that various groups have run different analyses based on independent approaches and routines

limitations_admitted.value: Photometric redshift uncertainties large; physical association flag may be a by-product of similar redshift distributions

evidence.quote: We note however that the uncertainties in the photometric redshifts used in this test are large.

referee_caveats_inferred: Sample overlap between classes makes classes not independent
Stacked flux measured as pixel maximum within 3'' (biased high)
ALESS pointings selected on bright SMGs so biased by design
SED fit has few data points, degenerate T and beta

data_public_as_stated.value: Data available from ALMA and ESO archives

evidence.quote: The data employed in this analysis are available from the ALMA and ESO archives.

missing_for_reproduction: Calibrated ALESS maps and Simpson et al. catalog needed
reproducibility.estimated_data_volume_inferred: ~tens of GB raw for 86 Cycle 0 pointings; much smaller if calibrated maps used
reproducibility.score_reason: Stacking recipe clear and data public, but inputs from companion papers and fitting details missing.
reproducibility.rediscovery_reason: Public data, simple stacking recipe, numeric results in tables; depends on companion catalogs.
